sourceEvidence.label: Sponsored onboarding, paymaster, private submission, and lifecycle evidence inventory

assessment.summary: Replace non-atomic account prefunding with signed ERC-4337 paymaster authorization and fail-closed private submission.

nonNegotiables: Sponsor authority never becomes account authority
Ambiguous private delivery never triggers automatic public fallback
Activation is nonce-zero and has empty account callData
assumptions: Production operators replace the reference in-memory ledger with a durable atomic store.
The selected private transaction provider is independently qualified before release.

opportunities.title: Make sponsorship atomic, bounded, and private-first
opportunities.summary: Use short-lived signed paymaster data and a private transaction route instead of prospective-account prefunding.
opportunities.diagnosis: Direct prefunding can strand user-controlled value, while a private browser-to-relay hop does not keep the sponsor transaction out of the public mempool.

evidence.claim: The old flow separated account prefunding from handleOps.
EntryPoint v0.9 requires direct EOA handleOps submission.
Paymaster validation bounds factory, operation shape, validity, policy, cost, and authorizer.
Private-first transport distinguishes explicit rejection from ambiguous delivery.

desiredInvariants: No sponsor value is deposited into a prospective user account.
An authorization cannot be replayed for another sender, factory, gas envelope, policy, or validity interval.
Budget is reserved before an authorization leaves the sponsor service.
Public fallback requires positive proof that private submission was not accepted.

options.title: Direct prospective-account prefund
options.summary: Fund the sender deposit and then submit handleOps.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Two independent transactions preserve stranded-fund risk.

tradeoffs.assessment: Partial failure can strand or duplicate sponsor value.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Force failure between deposit and handleOps.

options.title: Signed paymaster and private submission
options.summary: Authorize bounded gas sponsorship before the passkey signs and submit the final operation privately.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The bundler remains the direct EOA caller.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gas authority is bounded and separate from account authority.
Adds one authorization round trip but removes the prefund transaction.
Atomic charging and explicit fallback make retries decidable.
Requires deposit monitoring, durable quotas, and private-provider qualification.
Sponsorship is profile-selected and does not alter account authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Switch profile to counterfactual and verify self-funded activation.

residualRisks: Issued but unused authorizations reserve budget until operational reclamation.
A falsely advertised private provider can leak activation metadata.
Paymaster deposit owner remains an operational funding authority.

migrationNotes: No legacy wallets are supported; deploy a fresh profile.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Publish counterfactual onboarding policy and stop issuing sponsor authorizations.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the signed onboarding paymaster and private-first transport; keep counterfactual onboarding as the operator-selectable fallback mode.

openQuestions: Which durable store and authenticated principal system will each production integrator use?
Which private transaction provider will be qualified for the Sepolia release?
